avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce dofetilide levels and decrease antiarrhythmic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consult cardiology before discontinuation due to potential arrhythmia risk

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases dofetilide exposure and QT prolongation risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid entirely; potential for torsades de pointes

avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Hyperkalemia potentiates QT prolongation and increases torsades de pointes risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; monitor serum potassium (target 3.5-4.5 mEq/L); use only if clinically essential with frequent monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Hypomagnesemia increases QT prolongation risk; supplementation may be protective
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum magnesium levels; supplementation generally beneficial if deficient (target >2 mg/dL)

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases dofetilide levels and QT interval prolongation
avoid_foods.action: Avoid completely; no safe amount established

caution_foods.name: High potassium foods (bananas, spinach, tomatoes, oranges)
caution_foods.mechanism: Modest dietary potassium elevation may interact with renal function and QT effects
caution_foods.action: Monitor intake in patients with renal impairment; encourage consistent, moderate consumption

monitoring_notes: Dofetilide requires strict renal function monitoring (CrCl-based dosing) and baseline ECG with QTc interval <440 ms. Monitor serum electrolytes (potassium, magnesium, calcium) regularly, as electrolyte abnormalities significantly increase proarrhythmic risk including torsades de pointes.
